title: Approval ledger
description: An append-only record of approval decisions. Enforced by denial in v1: the ledger exists and nothing executes against it (FR-06, FR-58). The decider is recorded as a principal object identifier, never a display name or a configured label, so self-approval cannot be defeated by renaming (SEC-016). The agent's own principal is recorded on the ledger itself, which is what lets the self-approval check run offline against a single document instead of needing to correlate two.

agentPrincipalObjectId.description: The managed identity the agent runs as. Present so that a decider equal to this value is detectable within this document alone. A ledger that did not record it would push the self-approval check into a correlation step that could be skipped.

entries.description: Required, and required even when empty. An empty ledger records that nothing has been approved, which is a fact. An absent list would be indistinguishable from a ledger that was never written.

schemaVersion.description: The version of this schema the instance conforms to (FR-05, FR-29).

identifier.description: Lowercase, hyphen-separated. Constrained so an identifier cannot carry arbitrary text, and English by construction (FR-03, CON-01).

timestamp.description: RFC 3339, UTC, Z-suffixed. The pattern is present because format is an annotation by default.

sha256Hex.description: Lowercase hex, exactly 64 characters, as ADR-0004 pins.

principalObjectId.description: A directory object identifier, or a placeholder in the angle-bracket form that every shipped example uses. Admitting the placeholder form in the schema is what lets an example be both valid and free of a real identifier; without it, a valid example would have to contain one.

sequence.description: Position in the append-only sequence, starting at 1. That it increases by exactly one with no gaps is a semantic check; JSON Schema cannot compare array members.

previousEntryHash.description: The canonical hash of the preceding entry, forming a chain. Absent only on the first entry, which has nothing to follow. The chain is what makes a removed or reordered entry detectable: append-only is a property that has to be checkable, not merely promised.

approvedArtifactHash.description: The canonical hash of the artifact this decision applies to, not its name. Approving a proposal and then editing it yields a hash that no longer matches, so the approval does not silently carry over to the edited version.

decision.description: A recorded decision is one or the other. There is no pending value, because a pending decision is the absence of an entry rather than an entry.

deciderPrincipalObjectId.description: Who decided, as a principal object identifier. Never a display name: a display name can be changed to match, which would defeat the self-approval prohibition by renaming (SEC-016). That this value differs from agentPrincipalObjectId is a semantic check.

justification.description: Why. Optional for an approval and worth requiring by convention for a rejection, so the reason survives past the people who were present.
